questions.stem: What is the role of ontology in data integration and harmonisation?
options: To encrypt data in transit between systems
To describe structure and relations, enabling a coherent structure for data across systems, functions and domains
To schedule batch data pipelines
To replace all databases with a single system
To store backups of source data
questions.explanation: Ontology describes structure and relations, giving data a coherent structure across systems, functions and domains.

questions.stem: What do ontologies in data management involve?
options: A list of servers and their IP addresses
A set of SQL scripts for loading tables
A shared vocabulary and a set of relationships and rules to model a domain
A schedule of data refreshes
A directory of user permissions
questions.explanation: Ontologies use a shared vocabulary and a set of relationships and rules to model a domain, giving systems and stakeholders a common language.

questions.stem: Why is a new, ontological approach to data integration said to be needed?
options: Because cloud storage has become too expensive
Because regulators require ontologies
Because point-to-point integrations are no longer possible
Because the cost of maintaining point-to-point integrations and running specific data pipelines is growing
Because databases can no longer store relationships
questions.explanation: As the cost of maintaining point-to-point integrations and running specific data pipelines grows, an ontological approach makes cost control easier.

questions.stem: What is meant by semantic discrepancies as a data integration challenge?
options: Data sources using different file formats
Network delays between systems
Missing primary keys in tables
Duplicate rows in a dataset
Different interpretations of data across systems leading to inconsistencies and misunderstandings
questions.explanation: Semantic discrepancies arise when different systems interpret data differently, causing inconsistencies and misunderstandings.

questions.stem: What does semantic harmonisation ensure in ontology-driven integration?
options: That the meaning of data remains consistent across different systems
That all data is stored in the same physical database
That every table uses the same column count
That data pipelines run at the same time
That data is compressed uniformly
questions.explanation: Semantic harmonisation ensures the meaning of data remains consistent across different systems.

questions.stem: On the make-or-buy question for an ontology, what is the recommendation?
options: Buy a generic industry ontology and use it unchanged
The ontology needs to be made and developed specifically for each organisation
Use whichever ontology the database vendor provides
Avoid ontologies and rely on point-to-point mappings
Buy first, then discard it after a year
questions.explanation: Each company has a unique set of systems, semantics and functions, so the ontology must be made and developed specifically for each organisation.

questions.stem: What does the harmonisation process involve?
options: Deleting data that does not fit the target format
Migrating all systems to the cloud
Clarifying differences in data structures, formats and semantics to provide consistent, coherent semantics across the organisation
Replacing subject matter experts with automated tools
Encrypting all disparate sources
questions.explanation: Harmonisation aligns disparate data by clarifying differences in structures, formats and semantics so the organisation has consistent, coherent semantics.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as a benefit of ontology-driven integration and harmonisation?
options: Lower hardware costs for servers
Elimination of the need for data governance
Faster network bandwidth
Better decision-making because unified data leads to clearer insights
Automatic compliance with all regulations
questions.explanation: The benefits listed are improved data quality, efficient data management and better decision-making through unified data.

questions.stem: What recommendation is given for dealing with the complexity of ontology design?
options: Outsource the design entirely
Design the complete ontology before any use
Limit the ontology to a single domain forever
Skip the conceptual stage
Build it step by step rather than attempting a big-bang approach
questions.explanation: Developing a comprehensive ontology is complex and time-consuming, so the recommendation is to build it step by step and avoid a big-bang approach.

questions.stem: Why do ontologies require ongoing maintenance?
options: They need continuous updates and governance to remain relevant and useful
They expire under software licensing terms
They must be rebuilt after every database restart
They lose data when systems are backed up
They are stored only in memory
questions.explanation: Ontologies require continuous updates and governance to remain relevant and useful.
